report.currency: PHP (tables in PHP billions unless stated; ~USD at USD/PHP 64.05)
report.verdict: A 9M-26 print that is bad in level but no longer deteriorating: derived Q3 revenue of PHP 21.09bn (~$329m) was -15.8% YoY against -31.5% in Q2, with electronic-gaming revenue flat at ~PHP 9bn (~$141m) a quarter since the August-2025 e-wallet delinking reset the base. Net income of PHP 2.17bn (~$34m, -84.9%) reflects a structurally higher 5% PSC levy layered on a cost base that grew 3% while revenue fell 23% — the operating deleverage, not the court, is the bigger problem, and the FY26 H2 net-operating-income target now looks unattainable.
summary: **Headline — revenue down by a quarter, in line with PAGCOR's own reset.** 9M-26 total revenue PHP 64.41bn (~$1.01bn), -23.41% YoY from PHP 84.09bn (~$1.31bn); gaming-operations revenue PHP 58.13bn (~$908m), -23.44%. There is no sell-side consensus (PAGCOR is an unlisted, 100% state-owned GOCC chartered under PD 1869; FYE 31 Dec), so the relevant yardstick is PAGCOR's midyear FY26 revenue target of PHP 86.94bn (~$1.36bn): 9M is 74% of it.

**Net income collapsed 85%** to PHP 2.17bn (~$34m) from PHP 14.32bn (~$224m); net margin 3.4% vs 17.0%. Management attributes the sharper fall to the Supreme Court-mandated 5%-of-gross-income remittance to the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC). Our arithmetic says the PSC step-up explains only ~PHP 1bn (~$16m) of the PHP 12.15bn (~$190m) decline [estimate]; the rest is operating deleverage.

**Q3 standalone (our derivation, 9M less H1 — not company-reported):** revenue PHP 21.09bn (~$329m), -15.8% YoY and -0.6% QoQ; gaming revenue PHP 19.21bn (~$300m), -14.8%; net income PHP 0.59bn (~$9m), -83.5% YoY but +7% QoQ. The YoY decline has narrowed from -21.2% in Q1 and -31.5% in Q2 — the release does not say this.

**Electronic gaming is the entire story.** 9M e-games/e-bingo/bingo-grantee revenue PHP 27.63bn (~$431m), -37.23%; but the quarterly run-rate (Q1 PHP 9.21bn / Q2 9.39bn / Q3 9.03bn) has been flat within ±4% all year, i.e. a one-time base reset after the BSP's August-2025 e-wallet delinking order rather than continued erosion. E-gaming's share of PAGCOR gaming revenue fell to 47.5% from 58.0%.

**Land-based is holding.** Licensed casinos PHP 23.10bn (~$361m), -3.22%; PAGCOR-operated Casino Filipino PHP 7.28bn (~$114m), -8.0%; poker PHP 105.86m (~$1.7m), -4.6%. Licensed casinos are now 39.7% of gaming revenue vs 31.4% a year ago.

**Regulated-market GGR (PAGCOR's industry release, 6 Nov):** Q3 PHP 83.72bn (~$1.31bn), -11.41% YoY and -5.0% QoQ, moderating from -20.33% in Q2 and -15.87% in Q1; 9M PHP 259.45bn (~$4.05bn), c.-16% [our sum of the three quarterly releases]. Licensed casinos PHP 45.38bn (~$709m, -0.40%) took a record 54.20% share; e-gaming PHP 35.28bn (~$551m, -22.86%); PAGCOR-operated PHP 3.03bn (~$47m, -4.81%).

**Operating deleverage is the under-reported driver.** Total expenses PHP 19.86bn (~$310m), +3% YoY, against revenue -23%; net operating income PHP 44.55bn (~$696m), c.-31%; NOI margin 69.2% vs 77.1% (-790bps); derived Q3 NOI PHP 12.80bn (~$200m), margin 60.7% [expenses/NOI per Gaming Intelligence, sourced from PAGCOR's financial statements — the 9M press release omits lines the H1 release disclosed].

**PSC levy is structural and not yet fully in the P&L.** G.R. No. 223845 (Guiao v PAGCOR): the Court ordered 5% of gross income (before franchise tax and the 50% National Government share) from 1993 to date; reconsideration denied, reported final Jan-2026. 9M-26 PSC remittance PHP 3.01bn (~$47m); H1 was PHP 2.01bn, +58.7% YoY. Tengco (Aug-26) put arrears at ~PHP 37bn (~$578m) payable over 10 years with monthly remittances of up to PHP 700m (~$11m) — roughly PHP 8bn (~$125m) a year versus FY25 net income of PHP 17.47bn (~$273m).

**Contributions to nation-building** PHP 45.28bn (~$707m), -16.5% from PHP 54.26bn: National Treasury 50% share PHP 27.61bn (~$431m, -23.4%), socio-civic projects PHP 11.19bn (~$175m), PSC PHP 3.01bn, franchise tax PHP 2.90bn (~$45m, -23.5%), Casino Filipino host cities PHP 511.95m (~$8m), athlete incentives PHP 28.22m, corporate income tax PHP 15.85m (-97% from PHP 609.87m).

**Guidance bridge — FY26 target PHP 86.94bn (~$1.36bn), -18% vs FY25 PHP 106.03bn (~$1.66bn),** set at the midyear planning conference: H2 revenue PHP 43.62bn, H2 gaming PHP 40.76bn, H2 NOI PHP 31.28bn. After Q3, Q4 must deliver revenue PHP 22.53bn (~$352m; +6.8% QoQ, +2.7% vs Q4-25's PHP 21.94bn), gaming PHP 21.55bn (+12% QoQ) and NOI PHP 18.48bn (~$289m; +44% QoQ). Revenue is reachable only with a strong seasonal Q4; the NOI target is not credible at current cost run-rates.

**The one line running ahead of plan is net income:** the FY26 net-income projection of PHP 1.66bn (~$26m, -91% YoY) cited in secondary coverage of PAGCOR's budget has already been exceeded at 9M (PHP 2.17bn). This is a low bar, not a positive.

**Macro narrative is convenient but only partly true.** Management blames Middle East tensions/US-Iran conflict, oil and inflation for weak discretionary spending by lower-income e-games bettors; the peso closed at a record-low PHP 64.05/$ on results day after BSP's October rate hike and Brent's spike to $117. But the e-gaming base reset dates to the August-2025 delinking, before the oil shock.

**Regulatory overhang remains binary.** BSP ordered e-wallets/banks to remove in-app gambling links in Aug-2025; PAGCOR told the Senate online transactions fell ~50% within days and its income 40-50% in two weeks. Senate Committee on Games & Amusement (Tulfo) is still weighing ban-vs-regulate bills; PAGCOR is preparing a position paper asking BSP to restore links and plans a December-2026 app to steer players to licensed sites.

**Portfolio actions are defensive.** PAGCOR is weighing a sale of loss-making Casino Filipino branches, and at the Aug-26 congressional budget hearing pointed to CF asset sales and new streams (shared-services/back-office licensees, PHP 2.5-3bn, ~$39-47m, expected this year) to offset the PSC levy. The 2027 revenue target is PHP 88.34bn (~$1.38bn), +1.6%.

**Capital position: not disclosed.** The release contains no balance sheet or cash flow; cash, debt and leverage are n/a. As a GOCC there is no EPS, no buyback and no dividend — the statutory remittance stream (PHP 45.28bn at 9M) is the distribution.

**What management emphasises vs buries.** Emphasised: the e-gaming decline and the court ruling. Buried: Q3's sequential stabilisation, the 3% cost growth, NOI (disclosed at H1, dropped at 9M), the 9M-25 PSC comparative, and the 97% fall in corporate income tax.

**Comp-lapping sets up optically better Q4 prints.** Q4-25 revenue (PHP 21.94bn, ~$343m) and Q4-25 industry GGR (PHP 86.88bn, ~$1.36bn, derived) were the first full post-delinking quarters; at Q3 run-rates, Q4-26 would be roughly -4% YoY on both measures versus -16% and -11% in Q3.

**Thesis read-through.** For Entertainment City IR operators the data are benign — licensed GGR flat QoQ and share up 600bps YoY. For e-games licensees the industry base has found a floor around PHP 35-40bn (~$0.55-0.62bn) a quarter but faces a hostile legislative calendar. For the fisc, the National Treasury's take is down PHP 8.45bn (~$132m) YoY and the PSC claim is senior to it.

segments.name: Electronic Gaming (E-Games, E-Bingo, bingo grantees)
segments.headline: Down 37% YTD but flat for three quarters — the base has reset, the legislation has not.
narrative: They booked PHP 27.63bn (~$431m) of electronic-gaming licence revenue in the nine months, down 37.23% from PHP 44.03bn (~$687m), and this single line accounts for PHP 16.4bn (~$256m) of the PHP 19.68bn (~$307m) group revenue decline. Management framed it as the consequence of Middle East tensions and inflation squeezing lower-income bettors; the more complete explanation is the August-2025 order from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas requiring GCash, Maya and the banks to strip in-app gambling links, after which PAGCOR told the Senate that online transactions had halved within days and its own income had fallen 40-50% within two weeks. The comparison base therefore contains a July-2025 peak that no longer exists.

The quarterly cadence is the more useful read. PAGCOR's e-gaming revenue was PHP 9.21bn (~$144m) in Q1, PHP 9.39bn (~$147m) in Q2 and, by our derivation, PHP 9.03bn (~$141m) in Q3 — three prints inside a ±4% band, with Q3 down 24.9% YoY against PHP 12.03bn (~$188m) and only 3.8% QoQ. The segment's share of PAGCOR gaming revenue has fallen to 47.0% in Q3 from 53.4% a year earlier and 58.0% for 9M-25. In other words the step-down happened once, in the second half of 2025, and what remains is a flat, lower base rather than a continuing slide.

At the industry level the picture is marginally weaker. Regulated e-gaming GGR (e-games, e-bingo and bingo grantees) was PHP 35.28bn (~$551m) in Q3, down 22.86% YoY from PHP 45.73bn (~$714m) and 11.5% QoQ from PHP 39.85bn (~$622m); Tengco said the PHP 10.45bn (~$163m) decline accounted for the bulk of the industry contraction. Its share of total GGR slipped to 42.1% from 45.2% in Q2 and 48.4% a year earlier. That PAGCOR's own e-gaming revenue fell only 3.8% QoQ while industry GGR fell 11.5% lifts the implied take rate to 25.6% from 23.6% in Q2 (26.3% in Q3-25); we read this as fee-collection timing or product mix (e-bingo versus e-games carry different fee schedules) rather than a change in pricing, and would not extrapolate it. PAGCOR discloses no actives, ARPU, handle or promotional data for the segment.

The forward path is binary and political rather than operational. The Senate Committee on Games and Amusement continues to review bills ranging from an outright online-gambling ban to tighter regulation; BSP has said it will defer to Congress. PAGCOR, for its part, is preparing a position paper asking the central bank to restore e-wallet links and is targeting a December-2026 app that steers players towards licensed platforms — the stated logic being that delinking has pushed volume to illegal sites rather than eliminating it. There is no segment guidance, but the H2 gaming-revenue target of PHP 40.76bn (~$636m) implies PHP 21.55bn (~$336m) in Q4 after PHP 19.21bn in Q3; with e-gaming flat, that requires growth we do not see in the data.

segments.name: Licensed Casinos (integrated resorts & other licensees)
segments.headline: The anchor: licensed-casino GGR flat QoQ, -0.4% YoY, share up to a record 54.2% of the regulated market.
narrative: They collected PHP 23.10bn (~$361m) of licence-fee revenue from licensed casinos in the nine months, down 3.22% from PHP 23.87bn (~$373m); the segment is now the second-largest contributor to gaming revenue and its share has risen to 39.7% from 31.4% simply because e-gaming shrank around it. The first quarter was reported at PHP 7.62bn (~$119m), which leaves PHP 15.48bn (~$242m) for Q2 and Q3 combined, or roughly PHP 7.7bn (~$120m) a quarter — consistent with a stable implied take of ~17% on licensed-casino GGR. PAGCOR does not disclose Q2/Q3 segment figures and we treat the Q3 number as an estimate.

The industry data are the cleaner signal. Licensed-casino GGR was PHP 45.38bn (~$709m) in Q3, down just 0.40% YoY from PHP 45.56bn (~$711m) and flat on Q2's PHP 45.37bn (~$708m); for the nine months it sums to PHP 135.27bn (~$2.11bn). Share of total regulated GGR climbed from 50.83% in Q1 to 51.49% in Q2 and 54.20% in Q3 — a record, and 600bps above Q3-25 — which Tengco highlighted as evidence that the land-based base is holding. We agree with the characterisation: on a year in which the peso hit record lows and Brent touched $117, flat integrated-resort GGR is a respectable outcome, and it is the one part of the PAGCOR revenue stack that shows no sign of structural impairment.

The context for the small YoY decline is the full-year 2025 trend, in which licensed-casino revenue fell 4.93% to PHP 31.44bn (~$491m) against industry licensed GGR of PHP 182.50bn (~$2.85bn). The 9M-26 decline of 3.22% is therefore a modest improvement on the FY25 rate. PAGCOR gives no breakdown by VIP versus mass, by property or by Entertainment City versus provincial licensees, and no visitation or hold data, so we cannot say whether the resilience is volume or luck; the sequential stability across three quarters argues for the former.

There is no segment guidance. Mechanically, if licensed GGR holds at ~PHP 45bn a quarter, PAGCOR's licensed-casino revenue would land around PHP 30.8bn (~$481m) for FY26, roughly 2% below FY25 — which is the bull case for the whole P&L, since every other line is either falling or exposed to legislation. Management also pointed at the August budget hearing to fee income from new licensee categories, including shared-services/back-office operators (an MGM Resorts facility employing over 2,000 Filipinos was cited) worth PHP 2.5-3bn (~$39-47m) in 2026; this would be reported outside gaming operations and does not change the licensed-casino arithmetic.

segments.name: PAGCOR-operated Casino Filipino & Poker
segments.headline: Casino Filipino -8%, poker -5%, and the branch network is up for sale — a sub-scale operator inside a regulator.
narrative: They generated PHP 7.28bn (~$114m) from the Casino Filipino branches in the nine months, down 8.0% from PHP 7.91bn (~$123m), after PHP 2.64bn (~$41m) in Q1 and PHP 4.64bn (~$72m) across Q2 and Q3 combined. Poker, the smallest line, fell 4.60% to PHP 105.86m (~$1.7m) from PHP 110.97m (~$1.7m). The 9M decline is actually milder than FY25's 18.12% fall to PHP 10.38bn (~$162m), but that is a low bar: this is a government-run casino chain losing share to privately operated integrated resorts, and its H1 revenue was down 8.67%.

On the industry series, PAGCOR-operated casinos produced PHP 3.03bn (~$47m) of GGR in Q3, down 4.81% YoY from PHP 3.18bn (~$50m) but up 4.5% QoQ from PHP 2.90bn (~$45m); share of total GGR is 3.6%, versus 3.30% in Q2 and 3.16% for FY25. The 9M GGR of PHP 9.10bn (~$142m) against PAGCOR-reported CF revenue of PHP 7.28bn implies that ~80% of branch GGR is recognised as segment revenue, with the remainder presumably classified elsewhere (bingo at CF venues, for instance); PAGCOR does not reconcile the two series, and note that it has reclassified segment definitions between quarterly releases (poker was previously grouped with electronic gaming), so YoY comparisons on the industry series carry restatement risk.

The strategic question is whether the branches should exist. Trade press reports that PAGCOR has been weighing a sale of the Casino Filipino network as losses mount, and at the August congressional budget hearing management cited the sale of CF properties alongside new revenue streams as the offset to the PSC levy. The 9M release is silent on this, as it is on branch-level profitability, headcount or the PHP 511.95m (~$8m) paid to host cities. A disposal would be a one-off gain and a permanent removal of ~7% of gaming revenue; given the operating cost attached to the branches, it is likely NOI-accretive, but none of the economics are disclosed.

No guidance is provided for the segment. Our base case is continued mid-to-high-single-digit YoY decline — Q4 is seasonally the strongest quarter for the branches and the 'Big Time Bingo Milyonaryo' linked-bingo finale (PHP 13m, ~$0.2m, prize pool) on 6 December is marketing, not a swing factor. The watch item is whether a sale process is formally launched and how proceeds are treated under the statutory remittance formulae.

segments.name: Non-gaming revenue, cost base & statutory remittances
segments.headline: Costs +3% on revenue -23%; the PSC claim is now senior, structural and about to get larger.
narrative: Outside gaming operations they reported PHP 3.04bn (~$47m) from other related services, down 38.59% from PHP 4.95bn (~$77m), and PHP 3.23bn (~$50m) of other income (interest, fees), essentially flat on PHP 3.20bn. Combined non-gaming revenue of PHP 6.27bn (~$98m) was down 23.1%, and the derived Q3 figure of PHP 1.88bn (~$29m) was -25.0% YoY. The release offers no explanation for the services decline; the likeliest reading is that service fees scale with licensee activity in e-gaming. The corporate income tax line — payable on non-gaming income — fell 97% to PHP 15.85m (~$0.2m), which corroborates a sharp drop in taxable non-gaming earnings.

The cost side is where the release is thinnest. Per Gaming Intelligence, citing PAGCOR's financial statements, total expenses rose 3% to PHP 19.86bn (~$310m) and net operating income fell c.31% to PHP 44.55bn (~$696m), a 69.2% margin versus 77.1% a year ago; by subtraction Q3 opex was PHP 8.29bn (~$129m) and Q3 NOI PHP 12.80bn (~$200m) at a 60.7% margin, against 63.6% in Q3-25. PAGCOR disclosed NOI in its H1 release (PHP 31.75bn, -35.05%) but dropped the line at 9M. Whatever the reason, a cost base that grows while revenue falls by a quarter is the primary driver of the profit collapse: NOI fell PHP 20.26bn (~$316m), the National Treasury share fell PHP 8.45bn (~$132m) with it, and the residual gap to the PHP 12.15bn net-income decline is only partly the PSC.

The PSC obligation deserves precision because management leans on it. Under Section 26 of RA 6847 the Philippine Sports Commission is entitled to 5% of PAGCOR's gross income; from 1993 an executive order cut the effective rate to ~2.17%. The Supreme Court en banc (G.R. No. 223845, Guiao v PAGCOR, decision 22 Aug 2024) held the 5% is unqualified — computed before franchise tax and the 50% National Government share — and ordered an accounting and remittance from 1993 to date; PAGCOR's reconsideration bid, including its request for prospective-only application, was rejected and the ruling was reported final in January 2026. 9M-26 remittance was PHP 3.01bn (~$47m) (H1 PHP 2.01bn vs PHP 1.26bn, +58.7%). Tengco said in August that arrears of ~PHP 37bn (~$578m) are payable over 10 years and monthly remittances could reach PHP 700m (~$11m); on our arithmetic a 5% levy on ~PHP 88bn of 2027 revenue plus ~PHP 3.7bn of arrears amortisation is ~PHP 8bn (~$125m) a year — not yet in the run-rate, and larger than what is left of net income.

Total contributions to nation-building were PHP 45.28bn (~$707m), down 16.5% from PHP 54.26bn (~$847m): National Treasury PHP 27.61bn (~$431m, -23.4%), socio-civic projects PHP 11.19bn (~$175m), PSC PHP 3.01bn, franchise tax PHP 2.90bn (~$45m, -23.5%), host cities PHP 511.95m, athlete incentives PHP 28.22m and corporate income tax PHP 15.85m. Because the 50% share and franchise tax are formula-driven they fall with revenue, but socio-civic allocations and the PSC are not revenue-flexed in the same way, which is why net income absorbs a disproportionate share of any revenue decline. There is no balance sheet, cash-flow statement, debt or cash disclosure in the release; leverage is n/a. The relevant 'guidance' is the H2 NOI target of PHP 31.28bn (~$488m), which after Q3's PHP 12.80bn would require PHP 18.48bn (~$289m) in Q4 — a 44% sequential increase that the cost trajectory does not support.

blocks.heading: Non-gaming revenue
blocks.takeaway: Combined non-gaming revenue of PHP 6.27bn (~$98m) fell 23.1%, led by a 38.59% drop in other related services.
points: Other related services PHP 3.04bn (~$47m) versus PHP 4.95bn (~$77m); other income (interest, fees) PHP 3.23bn (~$50m), flat on PHP 3.20bn.
Derived Q3 figure of PHP 1.88bn (~$29m) was -25.0% YoY.
No explanation given; likeliest reading is service fees scale with licensee activity in e-gaming.
Corporate income tax fell 97% to PHP 15.85m (~$0.2m), corroborating a sharp drop in taxable non-gaming earnings.

blocks.heading: Cost base and NOI
blocks.takeaway: Total expenses rose 3% to PHP 19.86bn (~$310m) while NOI fell c.31% to PHP 44.55bn (~$696m), a 69.2% margin versus 77.1%.
points: Per Gaming Intelligence citing PAGCOR's financial statements; by subtraction Q3 opex PHP 8.29bn (~$129m), Q3 NOI PHP 12.80bn (~$200m) at 60.7% versus 63.6% in Q3-25.
PAGCOR disclosed NOI in H1 (PHP 31.75bn, -35.05%) but dropped the line at 9M.
A cost base growing while revenue falls by a quarter is the primary driver of the profit collapse.
NOI fell PHP 20.26bn (~$316m), National Treasury share fell PHP 8.45bn (~$132m); residual gap to the PHP 12.15bn net-income decline is only partly the PSC.

blocks.heading: PSC obligation
blocks.takeaway: The Supreme Court ruled the PSC's 5% of gross income unqualified; the levy is senior, structural and about to get larger.
points: Section 26 of RA 6847 grants 5%; a 1993 executive order cut the effective rate to ~2.17%.
G.R. No. 223845, Guiao v PAGCOR, decided 22 Aug 2024, ordered accounting and remittance from 1993; reconsideration rejected, ruling reported final January 2026.
9M-26 remittance PHP 3.01bn (~$47m); H1 PHP 2.01bn versus PHP 1.26bn, +58.7%.
Tengco said arrears of ~PHP 37bn (~$578m) are payable over 10 years and monthly remittances could reach PHP 700m (~$11m).
Our arithmetic: 5% on ~PHP 88bn of 2027 revenue plus ~PHP 3.7bn arrears is ~PHP 8bn (~$125m) a year, larger than remaining net income.

blocks.heading: Nation-building contributions
blocks.takeaway: Total contributions fell 16.5% to PHP 45.28bn (~$707m) from PHP 54.26bn (~$847m).
points: National Treasury PHP 27.61bn (~$431m, -23.4%); socio-civic PHP 11.19bn (~$175m); PSC PHP 3.01bn; franchise tax PHP 2.90bn (~$45m, -23.5%).
Host cities PHP 511.95m; athlete incentives PHP 28.22m; corporate income tax PHP 15.85m.
The 50% share and franchise tax are formula-driven and fall with revenue; socio-civic and PSC are not, so net income absorbs a disproportionate share of declines.

blocks.heading: Balance sheet and guidance
blocks.takeaway: No balance sheet or cash-flow disclosure; the H2 NOI target requires a 44% sequential Q4 increase the cost trajectory does not support.
points: No debt or cash disclosure in the release; leverage is n/a.
H2 NOI target PHP 31.28bn (~$488m) after Q3's PHP 12.80bn requires PHP 18.48bn (~$289m) in Q4.

highlights.text: Licensed-casino GGR flat QoQ at PHP 45.38bn (~$709m), -0.4% YoY, with share of regulated GGR up 600bps YoY to a record 54.2% — the integrated-resort base is intact despite a record-low peso and an oil shock.

E-gaming revenue has stopped falling sequentially: PAGCOR's quarterly e-gaming take of PHP 9.21bn / 9.39bn / 9.03bn (~$144m / $147m / $141m) is flat within ±4% across 2026; the August-2025 delinking was a one-time base reset.

Rate of decline is narrowing: derived Q3 group revenue -15.8% YoY vs -31.5% in Q2 and -21.2% in Q1; industry GGR -11.4% vs -20.3% in Q2. Q4 laps the first full post-delinking quarter (Q4-25 revenue PHP 21.94bn, ~$343m), implying roughly -4% YoY at current run-rates.

Other income held at PHP 3.23bn (~$50m, +0.9%), and derived Q3 net income rose 7% QoQ to PHP 0.59bn (~$9m); the FY26 net-income projection of PHP 1.66bn (~$26m) cited in budget coverage was already exceeded at 9M.

Implied PAGCOR take on industry e-gaming GGR rose to 25.6% in Q3 from 23.6% in Q2, cushioning PAGCOR's revenue (-3.8% QoQ) against an 11.5% QoQ drop in industry e-gaming GGR — likely timing/mix, but it helped the print.

Management is pursuing offsets with real numbers attached: shared-services/back-office licensees worth PHP 2.5-3bn (~$39-47m) in 2026, a Casino Filipino disposal, and a 2027 revenue target of PHP 88.34bn (~$1.38bn), +1.6%.

lowlights.text: The PSC levy is senior, structural and growing: 5% of gross income before franchise tax and the 50% government share, ~PHP 37bn (~$578m) of arrears over 10 years, monthly remittances of up to PHP 700m (~$11m) — roughly PHP 8bn (~$125m) a year from 2027 against FY25 net income of PHP 17.47bn (~$273m). Only PHP 3.01bn (~$47m) is in the 9M P&L.

Operating deleverage: expenses +3% to PHP 19.86bn (~$310m) on revenue -23%; NOI margin -790bps to 69.2% and a derived 60.7% in Q3. The cost base, not the court, explains most of the PHP 12.15bn (~$190m) net-income decline.

E-gaming revenue -37.2% to PHP 27.63bn (~$431m) and industry e-gaming GGR -22.9% in Q3; the Senate's ban-versus-regulate review is unresolved, BSP defers to Congress, and PAGCOR's position paper to restore e-wallet links has no timetable.

The H2 NOI target of PHP 31.28bn (~$488m) requires PHP 18.48bn (~$289m) in Q4 (+44% QoQ) and the H2 gaming target requires PHP 21.55bn (~$336m) in Q4 (+12% QoQ); neither is consistent with Q3 run-rates. Expect the midyear plan to be missed on profit even if revenue scrapes through.

Disclosure is thinning as results worsen: the 9M release omits NOI and expenses (disclosed at H1), Q3 standalone, the 9M-25 PSC comparative, any balance sheet or cash-flow data, and all operating KPIs (actives, ARPU, handle, hold).

Casino Filipino revenue -8.0% to PHP 7.28bn (~$114m), reportedly loss-making, with a sale under consideration but no process, valuation or timeline disclosed; host-city payments of PHP 512m (~$8m) continue regardless.

Other related services fell 38.6% to PHP 3.04bn (~$47m) with no explanation, and corporate income tax fell 97% to PHP 15.85m — a tell that non-gaming earnings have deteriorated more than the headline suggests.

forecast.intro: PAGCOR's only formal outlook is the FY26 plan set at its midyear planning conference: total revenue PHP 86.94bn (~$1.36bn), -18% versus FY25's PHP 106.03bn (~$1.66bn), split H1 actual PHP 43.32bn (~$676m) and H2 target PHP 43.62bn (~$681m); gaming revenue H2 PHP 40.76bn (~$636m); net operating income H2 PHP 31.28bn (~$488m). Nothing was formally changed at 9M, but the arithmetic has: after a derived Q3 of PHP 21.09bn (~$329m) revenue, PHP 19.21bn (~$300m) gaming and PHP 12.80bn (~$200m) NOI, Q4 must deliver PHP 22.53bn (~$352m) revenue (+6.8% QoQ, +2.7% YoY), PHP 21.55bn (~$336m) gaming (+12% QoQ) and PHP 18.48bn (~$289m) NOI (+44% QoQ). The shortfall is entirely the electronic-gaming division, whose H2-25 base management appears to have assumed would partially recover; licensed casinos are tracking plan. Separately, Tengco warned in June that FY26 industry GGR could fall as much as 19% (to ~PHP 321bn, ~$5.0bn); at the Q3 run-rate FY26 GGR lands near PHP 343bn (~$5.36bn), -13%, so that worst case is not materialising.

bridge.title: FY26 midyear-plan revenue target
bridge.change: -18.0% vs FY25; H2 PHP 43.62bn, H2 NOI PHP 31.28bn

bridge.title: 9M-26 actual
bridge.change: 74% of target; Q4 needs PHP 22.53bn (~$352m), +6.8% QoQ

bridge.title: Our FY26E revenue
bridge.change: -18.5% to -19.5%; slight miss, NOI miss larger

forecast.view: **Q4-26E revenue PHP 21–22bn (~$328–343m), roughly -4% to flat YoY** on seasonal land-based strength and a flat e-gaming base, giving **FY26E revenue of PHP 85.5–86.5bn (~$1.33–1.35bn), -18.5% to -19.5%** — a marginal miss of the PHP 86.94bn target. On profit we are well below plan: a Q4 NOI margin of 62–64% on PHP 21–22bn gives Q4 NOI of ~PHP 13–14bn (~$203–219m) and **FY26E NOI of ~PHP 57.5–58.5bn (~$0.90–0.91bn) versus the implied plan of PHP 63.0bn (~$984m)**; FY26E net income ~PHP 2.6–3.0bn (~$41–47m), -83% to -85%, with contributions to nation-building near PHP 60bn (~$937m). All figures are our estimates built from PAGCOR's reported 9M lines; no company model exists. **Leverage is n/a** — no debt or cash is disclosed and PAGCOR is funded by retained operating cash flow after statutory remittances. The 2027 setup is worse than 2026 on the bottom line even if revenue grows the targeted 1.6% to PHP 88.34bn (~$1.38bn): a 5% levy on gross income (~PHP 4.4bn, ~$69m) plus arrears amortisation (~PHP 3.7bn, ~$58m) is ~PHP 8bn (~$125m) of PSC outflow against a net-income run-rate of ~PHP 3bn, so either the statutory waterfall is reinterpreted, costs are cut materially, or reported net income goes to around zero. Swing factors, in order: a Senate decision on the online-gambling bills (ban would remove ~43% of gaming revenue; regulation with restored e-wallet rails could add 10–20% to the e-gaming base); a Casino Filipino disposal (one-off gain, permanent ~7% revenue loss, NOI-accretive); Q4 integrated-resort seasonality; peso/oil pass-through to mass-market spend.
watch: FY26 results (expected late Jan-2027): Q4 revenue vs the PHP 22.53bn (~$352m) implied target and whether NOI/expenses are disclosed again.
Q4-26 industry GGR release (expected Feb-2027): e-gaming GGR against the PHP 35–40bn (~$0.55–0.62bn) quarterly floor and licensed-casino share above 54%.

Senate Committee on Games & Amusement: progress of ban-vs-regulate bills; BSP response to PAGCOR's position paper on restoring e-wallet links; launch and uptake of PAGCOR's licensed-platform app (targeted Dec-2026).

PSC: the arrears accounting and payment schedule (~PHP 37bn over 10 years), whether remittances step up to ~PHP 700m/month in 2027, and any legislative attempt to amend RA 6847 or the PD 1869 waterfall.
Casino Filipino: formal launch of a sale process, perimeter, proceeds and treatment under statutory remittances; FY26 branch-level losses.
2027 corporate operating budget approval (GCG/DBM): revenue PHP 88.34bn (~$1.38bn) and the net-income line after full PSC compliance.
Macro: USD/PHP (record low PHP 64.05 on results day), Brent, BSP policy rate and the effect on mass-market discretionary spend at IRs and e-games.

report.sharePriceReaction: Not applicable — PAGCOR is an unlisted, 100% state-owned government corporation (chartered under PD 1869, as amended); there is no traded equity, EPS or share-price reaction. Read-across to listed Philippine e-games licensees and integrated-resort operators on 29 Oct 2026 was not verified.
report.confidenceNote: FX: USD/PHP 64.05 (BSP reference rate, 29 Oct 2026 — a record low for the peso); USD figures are approximate conversions. Headline 9M-26 figures (revenue, segment revenue, net income, remittances) are verified against PAGCOR's own release and at least four independent reports (Gaming Intelligence, Yogonet, GGRAsia, BusinessWorld, PNA). Q3-26 and Q2-26 standalone figures are our derivations (9M less H1; H1 less Q1) and are not company-reported; the Q3 licensed-casino revenue is an estimate. 9M operating expenses (PHP 19.86bn) and net operating income (PHP 44.55bn) are sourced only from Gaming Intelligence (citing PAGCOR's financial statements) and are not in the press release; 9M-25 NOI is back-solved. The FY26 net-income projection of PHP 1.66bn is secondary-sourced. The 9M-25 PSC remittance, quarterly 2025 industry e-gaming GGR, and any balance-sheet/cash-flow data were not found. The Yogonet URL was not directly accessible; its content was read via the search index and matched the PAGCOR release. Web-tool budget was exhausted before the Casino Filipino sale process and e-games licence-fee schedule could be independently verified; those points rely on AGB/BusinessMirror reporting.
